title: The Clock Without Hands
intent: A patient, suspended-time chamber miniature led by cello over still piano resonance.

tempo.feel: Slow 3/4 with broad legato phrases, flexible rubato at phrase endings, and occasional rests.

tonality.mode: major with minor-sixth shadowing and modal mixture

instrumentation.name: acoustic piano
instrumentation.role: Still harmonic backdrop; places three quiet chordal landmarks, later presents an inverted form of the cello motif.
instrumentation.timbre: Soft, resonant, widely spaced voicings with gentle attack and natural decay.

instrumentation.name: cello
instrumentation.role: Primary melodic voice; answers the piano with a descending lament figure, expands it into a long arch, then returns to the opening gesture.
instrumentation.timbre: Warm, intimate arco tone with restrained vibrato, sustained upper notes, and expressive legato.

structure.direction: Sparse piano establishes three quiet chordal landmarks in D-flat major, with unresolved stepwise bass motion and generous silence.
Cello answers with a descending lament figure and expands it into a longer arch. Keep the pulse broad, the counterpoint sparse, and dynamics restrained.
Piano briefly carries an understated inversion of the cello figure while cello sustains above, creating a calm, suspended convergence.
Return to the opening cello descent over thinning piano resonance. End in translucent major-minor ambiguity with natural decay.

production: Intimate acoustic chamber recording with close, clear separation between piano and cello, restrained natural room reverberation, warm cello presence, and spacious piano decay. Keep dynamics controlled and the perspective patient and unobtrusive. Clean studio recording, natural acoustic timbres, smooth transients and controlled peaks.
assumptions: Set a restrained 52 BPM to support the requested slow 3/4 pacing.
